title: Establish Hypercare Command Center
summary: Michelle recorded the Hypercare Command Center for the first 30 days of live operations (Monday 31 August 2026 00:00 America/New_York through Wednesday 30 September 2026 00:00). The plan defines a step-down monitoring cadence, a single issue-triage model mapped onto existing support P1–P4 / incident SEV-1–SEV-4 / defect critical–low scales, and daily (plus weekly) reviews. It uses the existing Launch-Day Runbook, Row 61 probes, Row 151 Launch Dashboard and Daily Founder Brief, Row 153 support, Row 83 social, and operating-system incident path. It does not create a second Founder dashboard, a new tracker, or a 24/7 overnight monitor. Founder acceptance is not recorded. August Launch row 208 is not marked Complete.

Row 61 production monitoring — Imani technical/risk ownership of probes and error ledger

Row 201 Confirm Launch Staffing and Coverage — Founder-gated broader staffing

Row 209 Launch-Day Executive Dashboard — separate Michelle deliverable; this CC uses Row 151 until 209 is accepted
Row 211 7-Day Executive Post-Launch Plan — September 1–7 owners/cadence (Command Center text). This CC does not close that row.
Row 212 30-Day Launch Performance Review Framework — targets, reporting, and corrective-action triggers. This CC is operating cadence, not the performance-review framework.

Define issue triage: intake, classification, routing, trackers, and daily triage inside the standup — without a new tracker product
Define daily reviews (morning standup + Daily Founder Brief + EOD close), weekly synthesis, Day-15 checkpoint, and Day-30 close
Map owners: Michelle chairs/coordinates; Imani owns tech/security monitoring and containment; Nia owns CX/support/social; Founder is escalation only

Create a second Founder dashboard or a new ticket/incident product

Execute go-live simulation (Row 206) or activate hypercare against live launch
Treat Kimberly Walker (AI) as execution capacity

hypercare_window.purpose: Keep operations, monitoring, triage, and Founder briefing running after launch day and after the first 72-hour window. Do not allow the command to fall off after stabilization.

Launch Health GREEN/YELLOW/RED and Founder Attention YES/NO

issue_triage.purpose: One classification and routing model for everything that arrives during hypercare: support tickets, production incidents, defects, launch risks, social handoffs, and privacy/security. Do not invent a third severity scale or a second informal tracker.
issue_triage.rule: Support priority is the Architect-ticket clock. Incident SEV is the production/risk clock. Defect severity is the release/fix clock. Classify all that apply. Map; do not stack new labels.

intake_sources.tracker: engagement log + one support ticket; not two cases

intake_sources.tracker: do not invent a second feedback product

support_priorities.published_architect_expectation: Typically respond within 3 days, with a goal of 72 hours or less. Do not promise a resolution time. Do not promise refunds.

incident_sev.SEV-1: CRITICAL — launch unavailable; payment broadly failing; material security/privacy; widespread access failure; material data-loss risk; severe participant-impacting production failure. Founder immediate.
incident_sev.SEV-2: HIGH — material degradation of important functionality or a meaningful participant cohort.
incident_sev.SEV-3: MODERATE — contained defect with workaround; no material launch threat.

defect_severity.critical: SEV-1 / must_fix_now during hypercare if the live surface is still blocked
defect_severity.high: SEV-2 / fix in the current hypercare window unless an accepted remaining risk is recorded

launch_health.RED: Open RED risk; website/registration/checkout/payment unavailable; open RED security/privacy/legal; open CRITICAL failure on a critical surface.
launch_health.YELLOW: Open YELLOW risk; elevated critical/high errors; support approaching/overdue 72-hour expectation; backlog ≥ 10; on/after launch day checkout starts with payment failures and zero purchases; data-quality ERROR; error ledger unavailable.
launch_health.GREEN: No RED/YELLOW. Missing error ledger cannot produce false GREEN.

support_to_incident_map.when: Broad outage, payment broadly failing, material security/privacy, widespread access failure, material data-loss risk, severe participant-impacting production failure.
Urgent ticket that is not a broad outage (contained individual security concern, or a payment issue affecting one Architect that is not a checkout outage).
Material degradation affecting important functionality or a meaningful participant cohort.
Contained individual defect with a workaround and no material launch threat.
Routine questions, feedback, cosmetic/non-critical. Do not open an incident for ordinary queue work.

routing.nia: preserves participant-facing evidence; no public secrets

routing.class: Payment ops (not a system outage): duplicate charge, cancellation, no-refund policy questions
